skills.definition: Finance refers to the ability to manage money, funding, and financial records so organizations can track resources, meet obligations, and support informed decisions. It includes understanding how transactions, budgets, and reporting connect to business performance and accountability.
skills.utilization: Accountants & Auditors use finance to record transactions, prepare statements, and verify that financial information is accurate and complete. They also apply finance to monitor compliance, explain results, and support reliable reporting for managers and external stakeholders.

skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can apply finance knowledge to reconcile accounts, review supporting documents, and prepare standard reports with limited supervision. They recognize common discrepancies, resolve routine issues, and maintain consistent records that support day-to-day accounting and audit work.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently apply finance practices to manage complex accounting tasks, evaluate financial records, and ensure reporting is accurate and compliant. They handle exceptions confidently, coordinate with others on financial issues, and produce dependable work that supports audits and decision-making.

skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently interpret financial statements across multiple reporting periods and use them to support dependable accounting and audit work. They can resolve routine reporting issues, validate presentation quality, and communicate findings clearly within established requirements.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.utilization: Accountants & Auditors use communication to explain financial findings, request supporting documents, and clarify accounting issues with colleagues, clients, and managers. They also communicate audit results, policy requirements, and deadlines in a way that supports compliance and informed decision-making.

They can confirm details, respond to common requests, and communicate simple accounting or audit updates without needing extensive guidance.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can explain standard accounting or audit matters to others, adapt their message to the audience, and handle common questions with confidence. They can summarize findings, coordinate follow-up actions, and communicate issues that require clarification while maintaining accuracy and professionalism.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can communicate complex accounting or audit information clearly, anticipate audience concerns, and adjust tone and detail to support understanding. They can lead discussions, resolve misunderstandings, and deliver reliable updates that help others act on financial information and compliance requirements.

It includes separating duties, authorizing transactions, and maintaining documentation so errors and irregularities are prevented or detected promptly.

skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can organize multiple administrative tasks at once, adjust priorities when schedules change, and keep records or correspondence updated with limited supervision. They coordinate routine office processes smoothly and help prevent delays by tracking details carefully.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently maintain complex office systems, balance competing priorities, and keep information, schedules, and materials organized across varied demands. They anticipate needs, adapt procedures when necessary, and ensure administrative work remains orderly and dependable.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Writing is the ability to effectively convey information, ideas, and thoughts through written communication. It involves organizing thoughts cohesively, using appropriate language and tone, and structuring content for clarity and impact.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use writing to prepare emails, memos, meeting notes, and routine correspondence. They also use it to record information accurately, relay instructions, and maintain clear communication across the office.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can write short, straightforward messages and fill in standard forms with basic accuracy. They can convey simple information clearly and use familiar templates or examples to complete routine written tasks.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can draft routine correspondence, summarize meetings, and adjust wording for different recipients with moderate confidence. They can organize information into clear paragraphs and correct common errors to keep communication professional and easy to follow.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can produce polished written materials that are accurate, concise, and well suited to the situation. They can tailor tone and structure for varied office needs, handle sensitive communication carefully, and maintain consistency across documents.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Data Entry refers to the accurate typing, recording, and updating of information into accounting systems, spreadsheets, or other records. It requires careful attention to detail so that names, dates, amounts, and reference numbers are entered consistently and can be retrieved without error.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use data entry to maintain calendars, contact lists, correspondence records, and office files. They also update routine information quickly so managers and coworkers can rely on current, accurate records.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can enter straightforward information into forms, spreadsheets, or databases with basic accuracy. They follow clear instructions, correct obvious errors, and keep routine records organized.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can handle recurring data entry tasks with fewer prompts and greater consistency across different record types. They check entries against source documents, resolve simple discrepancies, and maintain orderly files with limited supervision.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can manage data entry tasks reliably across multiple office systems while maintaining high accuracy and speed. They anticipate common record-keeping issues, verify information carefully, and keep administrative data current with minimal oversight.
skills.label: Durable Skill

They can add images or simple charts, refine layouts, and tailor slides for meetings or internal updates.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can produce polished presentations independently, organizing content for clarity, audience needs, and smooth delivery in administrative settings. They can combine multiple slide elements, maintain visual consistency, and revise materials quickly for managers or recurring office events.

skills.definition: Coordinating refers to the ability to align people, tasks, and timing so work moves smoothly toward a shared goal. It involves organizing priorities, communicating needs, and adjusting plans when conditions change.

They also align requests from managers, staff, and visitors so information and resources reach the right people on time.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can arrange simple schedules, pass along messages, and confirm basic meeting details with clear instructions. They handle routine coordination tasks accurately and know when to ask for help if plans change.

skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently coordinate complex schedules, competing requests, and recurring office processes while maintaining smooth communication across the workplace. They anticipate conflicts, adjust plans quickly, and keep managers and staff informed so operations remain organized and reliable.
skills.label: High Value Skill

skills.definition: Invoicing involves the creation and processing of invoices for goods or services provided, detailing the quantities, prices, and terms of the transaction.
skills.utilization: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants use invoicing to create and send invoices, verify basic billing details, and follow up on missing information or payment status. They also organize invoice records, route documents for approval, and help keep office billing processes orderly and timely.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can prepare straightforward invoices from provided information and check that names, dates, and amounts are entered correctly. They can file completed invoices, send them to the right recipient, and recognize obvious errors or missing details for correction.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can handle routine invoicing tasks with limited supervision, including matching invoice details to supporting records and resolving common discrepancies. They can manage multiple invoices at once, track basic payment status, and communicate professionally about routine billing questions.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently manage invoicing workflows, ensuring documents are accurate, complete, and sent on schedule. They can coordinate approvals, maintain organized records, and handle recurring billing issues reliably while keeping communication clear with clients and internal staff.
skills.label: Durable Skill

It includes keeping supplies organized, preventing shortages, and reducing waste through careful tracking and timely replenishment.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use office supply management to keep desks, meeting rooms, and shared work areas stocked and orderly. They coordinate routine replenishment, respond to requests for materials, and help ensure administrative tasks continue without interruption.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can identify common office supplies, check basic stock levels, and restock items from nearby storage. They follow simple instructions to report shortages, place supplies in the right locations, and keep shelves or drawers neat and accessible.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can track recurring supply needs, place routine orders, and organize inventory so frequently used items are easy to find. They notice patterns in usage, coordinate with vendors or internal contacts, and help prevent shortages before they affect daily work.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can manage office supplies reliably across multiple areas, balancing routine replenishment with changing office needs. They maintain organized inventory systems, anticipate demand, and coordinate ordering and distribution so administrative operations remain smooth and well supplied.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Time Management refers to the ability to plan, prioritize, and allocate working hours so tasks are completed on schedule and interruptions are handled without losing control of deadlines. It helps workers balance routine duties, urgent requests, and shifting demands efficiently.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use time management to coordinate calendars, prepare materials, and keep meetings, calls, and office tasks moving smoothly. They organize competing requests, maintain deadlines, and adjust schedules when priorities change.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can follow a daily schedule, complete routine clerical tasks on time, and respond to simple requests in the order received. They keep track of basic deadlines and use reminders to avoid missing appointments or filing dates.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can organize several recurring duties, shift priorities when urgent requests arise, and keep calendars and meeting preparations aligned. They manage their own workload with limited supervision and coordinate timing with coworkers to reduce delays.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently manage a full range of administrative deadlines, anticipate scheduling conflicts, and adjust plans to keep office operations on track. They reliably coordinate multiple priorities, maintain steady workflow, and ensure tasks are completed promptly and in the right sequence.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Problem Solving is the ability to identify, analyze, and solve complex issues or obstacles using logical reasoning and critical thinking skills.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use problem solving to manage scheduling conflicts, missing information, and communication breakdowns. They keep office tasks moving by finding workable solutions, clarifying needs, and adjusting plans when priorities change.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can recognize routine problems, follow established procedures, and ask for help when a situation is unclear. They handle simple issues such as correcting basic errors, locating missing documents, or redirecting routine requests to the right person.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can assess common office problems, compare a few practical options, and choose a response that keeps work on track. They resolve scheduling overlaps, clarify incomplete instructions, and coordinate with others to prevent small issues from becoming delays.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently handle varied administrative problems, adapt solutions to changing circumstances, and maintain smooth office operations. They anticipate likely disruptions, resolve conflicting demands, and make sound decisions that support reliable service and effective coordination.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Research involves systematically investigating a subject or phenomenon to discover new insights, validate existing knowledge, or solve specific problems. It includes gathering and analyzing information from various sources to draw meaningful conclusions.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use research to find contact details, verify schedules, gather background information, and prepare materials for meetings or correspondence. They use it to respond accurately to requests and keep office tasks moving smoothly.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can look up basic facts, locate simple documents, and confirm routine details using provided sources. They can gather information accurately when the task is straightforward and the needed answer is easy to identify.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can search multiple sources, compare results, and organize findings into a clear summary for supervisors or coworkers. They can handle routine requests with less guidance and choose information that is relevant and dependable.

They can sustain high-quality output across busy workloads while minimizing errors and preserving the intended meaning of each document.

skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently prepare and deliver polished presentations for varied administrative needs with confidence and consistency. They can tailor content to the audience, manage discussion smoothly, and represent office information clearly in formal or internal settings.

skills.definition: Travel Arrangements refers to the ability to plan, book, and coordinate transportation, lodging, and related details for business or personal trips. It includes confirming schedules, comparing options, and ensuring itineraries are accurate, practical, and aligned with traveler needs.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use travel arrangements to support executives and staff by organizing trips, reservations, and itinerary details. They coordinate with airlines, hotels, and transportation providers while keeping schedules, confirmations, and changes organized for smooth travel.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can make basic travel bookings and record simple itinerary details for a traveler. They follow clear instructions, confirm dates and times, and pass along reservation information accurately to the appropriate person.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can coordinate multiple travel components, such as flights, lodging, and ground transportation, with limited supervision. They handle routine changes, compare available options, and keep travelers informed of confirmed schedules and updates.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently manage complex travel arrangements for busy schedules and multiple travelers with consistent accuracy. They anticipate conflicts, adjust plans when changes occur, and maintain complete itineraries that support efficient and reliable travel.
skills.label: High Value Skill

skills.definition: Memos refers to the ability to draft, format, and distribute concise internal messages that communicate instructions, updates, decisions, or reminders clearly. It also includes choosing the right tone, organizing key points, and ensuring the message is easy for recipients to read and act on.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use memos to relay meeting changes, office procedures, and routine announcements to staff. They prepare messages that support smooth coordination, reduce confusion, and keep supervisors and team members informed in a timely manner.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can prepare simple memos from provided notes or templates and make basic edits for spelling, clarity, and format. They can distribute the memo to the intended recipients and confirm that the message is complete and readable.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can draft routine memos with minimal guidance, selecting appropriate wording for common office updates and instructions. They can organize information logically, adjust tone for the audience, and revise the memo to improve clarity before sending it.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently produce polished memos for varied office situations, tailoring content to the purpose, audience, and urgency of the message. They can anticipate needed details, maintain consistency with office standards, and ensure the memo supports effective administrative coordination.
skills.label: Durable Skill

It involves handling routine communication, supplies, and office procedures so staff can focus on core responsibilities.

skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can coordinate calendars, prepare routine correspondence, and manage common office supplies and records with limited guidance. They handle multiple administrative tasks at once and adjust priorities when schedules or requests change.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently oversee office routines, resolve scheduling conflicts, and maintain organized systems for documents, communication, and supplies. They anticipate administrative needs, keep operations consistent, and support the role with dependable judgment and efficiency.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Proofreading refers to the careful review of written material to catch spelling, grammar, punctuation, and formatting errors before documents are finalized. It helps ensure legal texts are clear, accurate, and professional, reducing the risk of mistakes that could affect understanding or credibility.
skills.utilization: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants use proofreading to check emails, memos, reports, schedules, and other office documents before distribution. This helps prevent mistakes, supports accurate communication, and presents a polished image for the office or manager.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can spot obvious spelling, punctuation, and formatting mistakes in routine documents. They can compare text against a source copy and make straightforward corrections before sending or filing the material.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can proofread a wider range of office documents with steady accuracy and notice less obvious errors in grammar, word choice, and layout. They can review drafts independently, correct common issues, and keep documents consistent with office standards.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can proofread complex or high-visibility documents reliably, catching subtle errors and inconsistencies before release. They can maintain a strong standard of clarity and professionalism across varied office materials while working efficiently with minimal oversight.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Expense Reports refers to the ability to prepare, review, and organize records of employee or business spending for reimbursement and accounting purposes. It includes checking receipts, matching expenses to policies, and ensuring entries are complete, accurate, and ready for approval.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants prepare expense reports for managers, staff, or visitors by gathering receipts and entering transaction details. They help ensure submissions are complete, timely, and aligned with office procedures before forwarding them for approval.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can collect receipts, enter basic expense details, and follow a simple reporting template with close guidance. They can identify missing items and route the report to the right person for review.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can assemble expense reports with limited supervision, verify entries against receipts, and correct common errors before submission. They can apply routine office rules, track pending approvals, and resolve straightforward questions from staff.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently prepare accurate expense reports for multiple people, handle exceptions, and ensure each submission follows office policy. They can coordinate with approvers and staff to resolve discrepancies quickly while keeping records organized and complete.
skills.label: High Value Skill

skills.definition: Scheduling involves creating and organizing a timetable or plan to allocate resources, tasks, or activities within a specified timeframe.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use scheduling to coordinate calendars, arrange meetings, and confirm availability for managers, staff, and visitors. They also adjust plans when changes arise, helping the office stay organized and responsive.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can enter appointments, update basic calendars, and follow clear instructions for setting meeting times. They handle simple scheduling requests and flag obvious conflicts or missing details for review.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can coordinate multiple calendars, resolve routine conflicts, and arrange meetings with several participants while keeping details accurate. They manage changes with limited supervision and communicate updates clearly to the people involved.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can independently manage complex scheduling across busy calendars, shifting priorities, and recurring commitments while keeping plans dependable. They anticipate conflicts, make timely adjustments, and maintain smooth coordination for the office without needing close oversight.
skills.label: Durable Skill

skills.definition: Front Office skill involves the ability to handle front desk operations efficiently, including tasks such as greeting visitors, answering phone calls, responding to inquiries, and directing individuals to the appropriate personnel or department.
skills.utilization: Secretaries & Administrative Assistants use front office skills to answer phones, welcome visitors, and route requests to the right person or department. They also help keep the office organized by handling basic information, providing scheduling support, and maintaining a professional first impression.
skills.level1: At Level 1 Proficiency, workers can greet visitors, answer routine calls, and pass messages accurately to the appropriate person. They follow standard office procedures, keep the reception area orderly, and respond politely to common questions using clear, basic communication.
skills.level2: At Level 2 Proficiency, workers can manage multiple front office tasks at once, such as screening calls, directing visitors, and coordinating routine scheduling requests. They handle common issues with confidence, adapt their communication to different people, and maintain steady service during busy periods.
skills.level3: At Level 3 Proficiency, workers can run front office activities smoothly and independently, balancing visitor flow, phone coverage, and administrative support with minimal supervision. They handle complex interactions professionally, resolve routine problems quickly, and ensure the office presents a consistent, reliable first impression.
